pages.text: Open $(thing)Transform$() and place one exact input in the upper slot. It stays visible until converted or returned. $(thing)Auto$() shows every compatible use of that item; choosing Fuel, Energy, Mana, or another produced target only filters those uses. Neither mode selects or consumes anything. Click one whole horizontal card, then use the upper ×1, ×8, ×64, or Max strip.

$(thing)Runtime Fuel:$() any item with a positive current $(thing)runtime burn time$() is accepted, including logs, datapack fuels, and compatible modded fuels. Each item adds that many Fuel ticks. Container items return normally, and an overflowing conversion leaves the input untouched.

$(thing)Brew Energy:$() Blaze Rod adds 1,200 and Blaze Powder adds 600. A Blaze Rod may therefore show both Fuel and Brew Energy cards in Auto. The player chooses the conversion; there is no hidden priority.

$(thing)Axe Energy:$() an accepted axe is consumed. Finite value comes from remaining $(thing)durability$() × ($(thing)Unbreaking$() level + 1) × stack count; Mending adds nothing. An $(thing)Unbreakable$() axe supplies infinity. Supported strip, scrape, and wax-off recipes spend one Axe Energy each.

Some modded transforms are timed. For example, a generator can convert fuel into FE only after its installed processing station has accumulated enough work at that exact variant's rate. Storage container transfer is not a transform: batteries, tanks, and Mana containers use direct deposit or withdrawal instead.

The target sidebar is always visible. Search uses localized produced-resource names, arrows or the wheel change pages, and middle-click returns to Auto. Every card names its direct source or required station and work on its second line; selection uses the card's inset state instead of a separate lower preview.
